D.t: Maura Healey leads by 27.2 in the forecast and wins 100% of simulations. The cushion is about 777,886 votes; a one point swing is about 14,284 voters changing sides.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between D +19.7 and D +34.6. Only an unusual polling error changes the winner.
The polls page average is D +22.0. Your best recent poll is UMass Amherst/WCVB/YouGov at D +24.0; your worst is University of New Hampshire at D +16.3. 4 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Middlesex, a projected net 289,897 votes; Suffolk, a projected net 165,139 votes; Norfolk, a projected net 90,139 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Worcester, D +9.0, 11.8% of the vote; Plymouth, D +6.3, 8.4% of the vote; Bristol, D +6.5, 7.6% of the vote; Hampden, D +6.3, 5.8% of the vote.

D.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
D.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Maura Healey runs furthest behind in Hampden, Plymouth, Essex. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: White voters, 77% of voters, 57 to 42, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.86 points; Men, 46% of voters, 57 to 41, where a 5 point gain is worth 2.29 points; Voters without a degree, 44% of voters, 60 to 38, where a 5 point gain is worth 2.23 points.

The forecast's worst groups for Maura Healey: Immigration voters 37 to 61, Voters who can afford daily costs 55 to 43, White voters 57 to 42. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$6.9M cash against $1.5M. Spend it early on persuasion television in the battleground counties and keep a reserve for the last week.
